scenes.title: Two Stanford GRE test booklets side-by-side — identical inside, differing only by the Page-1 'Diagnostic Ability' vs 'Problem-Solving Puzzle' cover
scenes.era: 1995, Stanford University testing classroom, Palo Alto, California

layout.description: Sunlit 1995 Stanford lecture room with oak tablet-arm desks holding two side-by-side 30-minute GRE verbal test packets and No. 2 pencils in front of a chalkboard timer.

positions.who: Claude Steele & Joshua Aronson (mannequins in 1995 blazer and collared shirt)
positions.where: standing beside the front desk comparing the two cover sheets that unlock vs hijack equal SAT-matched students
rubbing temples tensely over Question 4 after checking a Page-1 demographic box, working-memory scratchpad crowded
working smoothly and briskly through the exact same GRE passages with full focus

props.name: Packet A ('DIAGNOSTIC INTELLECTUAL ABILITY TEST' + Page-1 Demographic Box)
props.period_detail: cream 1995 test cover with demographic bubble right above Question 1
props.physical_behavior: triggers anxious self-monitoring that steals working memory

props.name: Packet B ('NON-DIAGNOSTIC PROBLEM-SOLVING STUDY' — Demographics on Last Page)
props.period_detail: identical interior GRE verbal items with clean Page 1
props.physical_behavior: allows SAT-matched cohorts to perform equally

props.name: adjusted SAT-matched score bar chart
props.period_detail: crisp white placard showing the artificial gap appearing ONLY under Diagnostic / Page-1 priming and closing under Non-Diagnostic framing

actions.verb_sequence: checks the Page-1 demographic box -> reads 'measures innate ability' -> hesitates and double-checks simple lines repeatedly as the 30-minute clock ticks
swaps the cover sheet to Packet B ('Problem-Solving Mechanics') and moves the demographic sheet to the very back -> Test-Taker B solves items cleanly at full capacity

reactions.reaction: points out every single GRE word inside both booklets was 100% identical
finishes the final passage with calm concentration

scenes.wardrobe: 1995 Stanford attire: tailored tweed/navy blazer over open shirt on researchers; collegiate sweatshirts, button-downs, and denim on students.
scenes.recognition_hook: Every tough GRE question inside both packets was identical — changing one sentence on the cover page or moving one checkbox to the back changed how much working memory walked into Question 1.

key_visual.description: two 1995 Stanford researchers comparing two GRE test booklets ('Diagnostic Ability' with Page-1 checkbox vs 'Problem-Solving Study') across sunlit classroom desks

scenes.title: White male math majors hit by the exact same threat in 1999

layout.description: Bright math exam room where high-SAT White male math students receive a cover note mentioning an 'Asian vs White math comparison'.

positions.where: pausing tensely mid-equation as anxious self-monitoring steals calculus RAM

props.name: calculus problem sheet
props.physical_behavior: demonstrates stereotype threat is a universal human cognitive tax

actions.verb_sequence: reads comparison header -> second-guesses steps and runs short on time

reactions.reaction: confirms any valued identity can experience working-memory drag

scenes.recognition_hook: Even top-scoring White male math majors dropped on calculus the instant a cover note cued a comparison stereotype.

scenes.title: College Board moving demographic bubbles to the END of the exam

layout.description: Clean exam-design table showing 'Demographics' moved from Page 1 behind the final 'STOP — Test Complete' page.

positions.where: sliding the demographic form behind the final test page

props.name: reordered exam packet ('Questions First -> Demographics Last')

actions.verb_sequence: places demographic bubbles after the last question

scenes.recognition_hook: Moving one demographic page from the front cover to the back cover costs zero dollars and protects working memory.

scenes.title: Delivering 'Wise Feedback': High standards + explicit belief

layout.description: Sunlit office table where a mentor hands back an essay marked with detailed margin edits AND a clear top note: 'High standards + I know you can reach them.'

positions.where: pointing constructively to margin notes and the encouraging standard card
leaning in energized to revise the draft without defensive threat

props.name: essay draft with 'High Standards + Full Confidence' header

actions.verb_sequence: frames tough critique as belief in high potential -> Student dives eagerly into edits

scenes.recognition_hook: Tough standards paired with 'I know you have what it takes' unlocks prefrontal focus instead of defensive alarm.
